# Go Instructions

These instructions define the coding conventions for Go in this workspace.

## Language Version

Go 1.24.0 (module: github.com/softwaresalt/backlogit)

## Error Handling

- Wrap errors: `fmt.Errorf("context: %w", err)`  
- Sentinel errors for known failures
- Typed errors for domain categories
- Never ignore returned errors
- No `panic()` in library code; return errors to the caller instead
- Do not use silent success-shaped fallbacks that swallow a real failure

## Naming Conventions

- Exported: `PascalCase`, Unexported: `camelCase`  
- Acronyms all-caps: `ID`, `HTTP`, `URL`, `SQL`, `MCP`  
- Interfaces: single-method use `-er` suffix
- Packages: short, lowercase, no underscores
- Keep receiver names short and consistent across a type's methods (e.g., `s *Server`)

## Code Organization

- Follow Go standard project layout: `cmd/` for entry points, `internal/` for private packages
- One package per directory, package name matches directory name
- No circular imports — use interfaces at package boundaries
- Keep packages focused: each package should have a single responsibility
- Group by responsibility (`internal/core`, `internal/db`, `internal/mcp`, `internal/events`), not by type
- Keep package boundaries aligned with the CQRS split between the Markdown source of truth and the SQLite cache

## Documentation

- Doc comments on all exports starting with identifier name
- Package doc in `doc.go` for non-trivial packages

## Testing

- Unit tests in `*_test.go` colocated with source
- Integration tests in `tests/`  
- Table-driven tests with `t.Run`  
- Use `testify/assert` and `testify/require`
- Cover MCP tool schemas, outputs, and error behavior; rehydration/index rebuild behavior; and queue, stash,
  dependency, and migration logic when those areas change

## Dependencies

- Pin all dependencies in `go.mod` with exact versions
- Run `go mod tidy` after adding/removing imports
- Prefer standard library over third-party when feasible
- Vendor dependencies if reproducible builds are required

## Safety & Security

- No `unsafe` package without explicit justification
- Validate all external inputs
- Use parameterized SQL queries
- Guard goroutines with lifecycle management
- Reject unsafe path construction; use canonical path handling and reject path traversal or untrusted relative paths
- Prefer explicit type assertions or conversion helpers over `fmt.Sprintf("%v", value)` coercion at
  `map[string]any`/YAML-decoded boundaries
- Pass `context.Context` explicitly to I/O or blocking work

## Performance

- Pre-allocate slices when length known
- Use `strings.Builder` for concatenation
- Profile hot paths with `pprof`
- Use parameterized SQL queries and existing indexes rather than full-table scans in `internal/db`

## Anti-Patterns

The following patterns are prohibited:

- Avoid `init()` functions — use explicit initialization
- Avoid global mutable state — prefer dependency injection
- Avoid `interface{}` / `any` when concrete types or generics suffice
- Avoid returning error + bool — return only error
- Avoid deep package nesting — prefer flat package layout
- Avoid `fmt.Println` or ad hoc logging in place of `log/slog`
- Never bypass the read-only gate around `backlogit_query_sql`
- Never write outside the intended workspace root or the backlog storage boundary
